headline: China's National Parks Bring Wildlife Back from Brink
meta_description: Since 2021, China's five national parks have sparked a wildlife revival. Siberian tigers tripled and Amur leopards nearly tripled in number.
summary_short: China's five national parks are delivering results. Siberian tigers jumped from 27 to 72, while Amur leopards rose from 42 to 115 since 2021.
body:
China's five national parks, established in 2021, are succeeding at one of conservation's hardest tasks: bringing endangered species back from the edge of extinction.

The numbers tell a striking story. Siberian tiger populations have nearly tripled, climbing from just 27 to 72. Amur leopards—among the world's rarest big cats—surged from 42 to 115. Even more dramatic: Tibetan antelope herds rebounded from under 20,000 to over 70,000.

These aren't abstract conservation metrics. Each number represents a living animal reclaiming habitat, breeding, and surviving in the wild. The parks are proving that when governments commit serious protection to vulnerable ecosystems, wildlife responds. For species that once seemed headed toward extinction, these numbers offer something increasingly rare in our time: genuine hope.
quick_facts: Amur leopards: 42 to 115 in same period
Five national parks established in China in 2021
Major success in endangered species recovery
